To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The SINR of a user terminal can be tightly and accurately approximated as a weighted sum of independent non-central chi-squares, (ii) the sum rate of the massive multiple-input multiple-output system can be accurately approximated as the sum of weighted non-central chi-squres, and (iii) the proposed approximations are accurate across a variety of spatial correlation models, Ricean K-factos, and average uplink signal to noise ratios

the instantaneous SINR of an arbitrary user can be approximated as a linear combination of scaled non-central chi-squares, and the statistical moments of the SINR, as well as system sum spectral efficiency, can be approximated using the moment generating function of the SINR.

the MMSE SINR of an arbitrary user can be tightly approxi- mated by a linear combination (with scaling factors depending on the link gains, K factors and eigenvalues of correlation matrices) of non-central chi- squared random variables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient framework for the evaluation of the performance of massive MIMO systems with minimum-mean-squares-error processing, under heterogeneous propagation conditions.

the performance analysis of a massive MIMO system with minimum-mean squared-error processing, under the most general spatially correlated Rice fading channel, with heterogeneous K-factors and spatial correlation matrices across all terminals.
the development of an analytical framework to approximate SINR and sum rate for massive MIMO with heterogeneous Ricean fading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SINR is a linear combination of the non-central chi-squares.

the SINR and system spectral efficiency of the massive MIMO uplink can be accurately approximated by a combination of chi-square random variables, with a tight approximation for their first and second moments, and the accuracy of the approximation is independent of the spatial correlation models, link gains and K-factors.
the SINR and the sum spectral efficiency of a massive MIMO system with MMSE processing can be approximated with a high accuracy under a fully heterogeneous setting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MMSE receiver is an attractive solution for massive MIMO systems operating in heterogeneous propagation conditions.

, the proposed framework can be applied to a wide range of massive MIMO systems, where each terminal has a distinct propagation channel, and it provides a tight approximation for the SINR and the sum spectral efficiency.

, for the considered massive MIMO system, the SINR of an arbitrary user is tightly approximated by linear combinations of non-central chi-square random variables and the statistical moments of the SINR, and hence, of the spectral efficiency, can be accurately approximated using a novel analytical methodology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of massive MIMO systems is not necessarily dominated by the strongest link in the system, as is often assumed.

the SINR and the sum spectral efficiency can be tightly approxim- ated by simple expressions, that can be readily used to evaluate the performance of a massive MIMO system under a wide range of practical conditions.
, despite the heterogeneity, the system performance is well approximated by the performance under the special case of homogeneous propagation conditions.
